_description: Source registry for Canadian utility rate scrapers. Each entry maps a utility to its data sources and scraper implementation.

utilities.name: Enbridge Gas

sources.description: Residential natural gas rates for the Enbridge Gas Distribution service area
Commercial and industrial natural gas rates

utilities.notes: Enbridge Gas Inc. was formed by the merger of Enbridge Gas Distribution and Union Gas in 2019. Rates vary by rate zone (former EGD vs. former Union Gas territories). Regulated by the Ontario Energy Board (OEB).

utilities.name: Énergir

sources.description: Pricing page that links the current Conditions of Service and Tariff edition

Conditions of Service and Tariff as of October 1, 2026: supply, transportation, load balancing, Rate D1, renewable-gas socialization and cap-and-trade prices (link is rediscovered from the pricing page each run)

utilities.notes: Énergir (formerly Gaz Métro) is the principal natural gas distributor in Quebec. Regulated by the Régie de l'énergie du Québec. Default Rate D1 is parsed live for residential and business listings: seven annual-volume basic-fee bands, nine daily distribution blocks, supply, transportation, conditional load balancing and renewable-gas socialization, and the cap-and-trade (CTEAS) price, all in native cents/m3 stored as $/m3. Rates D3 and D4 (subscribed-volume minimum daily obligation bands, withdrawal prices, eligibility thresholds) are parsed from article 14.3 of the same tariff. Interruptible D5, inventory-related adjustments, the load-factor balancing formula, rate reductions and fixed-price/renewable supply options remain gaps.

utilities.name: FortisBC Energy

sources.description: Rate 1 residential tables for Mainland/Vancouver Island and Fort Nelson
Rate 2 and Rate 3 commercial tables and annual-volume eligibility
Province of British Columbia notice that carbon tax was eliminated effective April 1, 2025; required carbon evidence
Rate Schedule 5 General Firm Service (Mainland/Vancouver Island); link rediscovered from the business rates page
Rate Schedule 4 Seasonal Firm Gas Service; link rediscovered from the business rates page

utilities.notes: FortisBC Energy is the natural gas distribution arm of FortisBC, serving most of British Columbia. Regulated by the British Columbia Utilities Commission (BCUC). Rates 1/2/3 are parsed live for Mainland/Vancouver Island and Fort Nelson with daily basic charges and $/GJ delivery, storage and transport and cost of gas; Rate 5 (monthly basic, $/GJ/month daily-demand charge, riders) and Rate 4 seasonal (off-peak/extension periods) are parsed from their approved rate schedules for Mainland/Vancouver Island. Missing carbon evidence rejects live output. Fort Nelson Rates 4/5 (no published price table), Revelstoke propane, Rates 6/7 and Customer Choice marketer prices remain gaps.

utilities.name: Centra Gas Manitoba

sources.description: Current residential Centra gas basic, commodity and delivery components
General-service and large-volume gas Sales/T-service class tables and native demand units
Default quarterly commodity rate and marketer-supply applicability
Dated federal zero fuel-charge applicability naming Manitoba; required for complete carbon evidence

utilities.notes: Twelve current residential/commercial Sales, T-service and marketer-supply variants. Source cents/m3 are normalized to dollars/m3, without heat-content conversion; native volumetric demand units and component dates are preserved. Delivery/demand totals are checked against their parts, not added twice. Private marketer commodity is excluded and explicit carbon evidence is mandatory. Fixed-term products, full PUB tariff/eligibility and alternate-supply conditions remain review gaps; no full catalogue-completion claim.

utilities.name: SaskEnergy

sources.description: Residential full-service and delivery-only basic, delivery and commodity charges
Commercial volume classes and full-service/delivery-only charges; small industrial still needs scope and component audit
Required dated carbon applicability and explicit zero charge for residential/commercial service
Eligibility for delivery-only service; private retailer commodity prices are not included

utilities.notes: Six live residential/small-commercial/large-commercial full-service and delivery-only variants. Base charges are published effective October 1, 2023; the assembled tariff begins April 1, 2025 when its separately dated, source-verified zero carbon component applies. Missing carbon evidence rejects live output. Private retailer commodity prices are excluded from delivery-only records, not invented. Small industrial eligibility and billing fees/municipal payments remain audit gaps; no full building-catalogue completion claim.

utilities.name: Heritage Gas

sources.description: Residential rate summary (Eastward Energy, formerly Heritage Gas); cross-checked against the rate table
Commercial class definitions, General Service summary and the 'View Rates' link to the monthly rate table
October 2026 rate table: fixed, base energy (GS tiers), TCRR, GCRR, RDA, zero federal carbon note and municipal riders (link is rediscovered monthly)
Approved tariff (linked as 'Tariffs' on https://eastwardenergy.com/regulatory/): Rate Class 3 demand charge unit ($/GJ of Billing Demand per month), billing-demand rule and eligibility

utilities.notes: Eastward Energy (formerly Heritage Gas) distributes natural gas in Nova Scotia. Regulated by the Nova Scotia Energy Board (formerly NSUARB). Residential, General Service and Rate Class 3 are parsed live from the monthly rate table and must agree with the page summaries (RC3 with the approved tariff, which defines its demand-charge unit and billing demand); the table's own dated zero federal carbon note is required. Rate Class 4 rates are negotiated per site and not published.

utilities.name: Liberty Utilities NB

sources.description: Distribution rates for all six classes and SGS/MGS/LGS rate schedules (effective January 1, 2025)
Liberty Utility Gas commodity rate history ($/GJ); current month required for SGS
Liberty Utility Gas commodity rate history ($/GJ); current month required for MGS/LGS
Dated federal zero fuel charge and New Brunswick's charge period ending March 31, 2025; required carbon evidence

utilities.notes: Liberty Utilities acquired the former Enbridge Gas New Brunswick operations. Regulated by the New Brunswick Energy and Utilities Board (NBEUB). SGS, MGS, LGS and Off-Peak Service are parsed live with alternative customer charges, monthly delivery blocks, LGS seasonal excess-volume rates, the current Liberty Utility Gas commodity and required zero-carbon evidence. Process-load CGS/ICGS are non-building exclusions; marketer prices are not included.

utilities.name: BC Hydro

sources.description: Residential tiered (Step 1/Step 2) electricity rates sub-page
Residential electricity rates landing page
Optional residential flat rate RS 1151
Optional RS 2101 time-of-day pricing with either tiered or flat base service
Authoritative residential RS 1101/1105/1151/2101 and riders 1901/1904, with dates and conditions
Commercial electricity rate schedules (SGS, MGS, LGS)

utilities.notes: BCUC-regulated residential choices include tiered 1101, flat 1151, each with optional 2101 time-of-day, plus closed dual-fuel 1105. The live parser reads the approved PDF including dates, separate 1901/1904 riders and conditional transformer discounts; the riders exclude 2101 adjustments. Business parsing remains separate.

utilities.name: FortisBC Electric

sources.description: Approved Electric Tariff; current RS 1/2A/20/21/22A/23A dates, rates, conditional credits and demand alternatives
Residential electricity rates for FortisBC Electric service area in southern BC interior
Commercial electricity rates

utilities.notes: Six live January 2026 building schedules: flat RS 1, closed residential TOU 2A, commercial 20/21 and TOU 22A/23A. Per-two-month and per-month charges remain native; RS21 kW/kVA components are alternative bases. Conditional voltage/transformation credits are negative rebates, not additive charges. Large commercial 30-33/37/38, Green Power85, financing91, net-metering95 and EV96 remain audit gaps. PDF extraction selects source sheets by printed footer to avoid table-of-contents extraction stalls.

utilities.name: Hydro-Québec

sources.description: Residential Rate D (standard domestic rate) with tiered pricing
Domestic demand Rate DP; values and seasonal billing rules are parsed from the approved PDF
Grandfathered bulk-metered domestic Rate DM; eligibility and multiplier rules retained
Official electricity rates PDF: D/DP/DM/DN/DT/Flex D, closed Winter Credit option and G/M; page-aware domestic eligibility, multipliers, temperature/event rules and conditional credits
Business rate schedules landing page (JS-rendered, links to PDF)

utilities.notes: Nine live records include D/DP/DM/DN/DT/Flex D, the closed Winter Credit adjustment and G/M. DT switches on source-defined outdoor temperature zones, not hourly TOU, and excludes off-grid service. Flex D preserves seasonal tiers, notified events and mutually exclusive product eligibility. Winter Credit is a conditional adjustment to Rate D, retaining reference-energy rules and enrollment cutoff. Multiplier, minimum-bill and demand rules remain conditions, not calculated bills. Inukjuak, net metering and remaining building business options still need audit; no full catalogue-completion claim.

sources.description: Residential electricity rates including basic charge and energy charge
Commercial and industrial electricity rates

utilities.name: SaskPower

sources.description: Residential and commercial power supply rates for Saskatchewan
Residential standard E01/E03, closed-to-new bulk-metered application, and diesel E04
SaskPower-supplied transformation: E05/E06, E75/E76, E37 irrigation, E15-E18 unmetered and E35 diesel
Customer-owned transformation: standard, small commercial, power TOU, power standard and capacity reservation
Renewable Access Service R23/R24: self-generation eligibility, voltage-specific charges and billing-demand conditions
Farm standard, irrigation and closed-to-new interruptible irrigation: E34, E19, E41
Oil-field supplied/customer-owned standard, high-voltage and time-of-use: E43/E44, E46-E48, E86-E88

utilities.notes: SaskPower is a provincial Crown corporation regulated by the Saskatchewan Rate Review Panel. The October 1 building-schedule audit is implemented: standard/bulk-metered/diesel residential, supplied/customer-owned general service, power/TOU/capacity and R23/R24 renewable access. The 41 live records include completed non-building reference classes. Partial status reflects the broader catalogue; standalone lighting and reseller schedules are outside the building completion scope. Published net rates exclude applicable taxes and surcharges.

utilities.name: NB Power

sources.description: Residential electricity rates
Business electricity rates

utilities.notes: NB Power is a vertically integrated Crown corporation and the primary electricity provider in New Brunswick. Regulated by the New Brunswick Energy and Utilities Board (NBEUB). Rural/Seasonal residential, residential and business water-heater rental, SureConnect, Recreational Lighting and Public Fast Charging are parsed live from the two official rate pages (effective April 14, 2026, parsed from the pages). Small/Large Industrial, lighting and one-time fees (published under a "$/month" heading) are excluded/not modelled. General Service II was merged into General Service I on April 1, 2025.

utilities.name: Nova Scotia Power

sources.description: Standard residential rates with actual rate values (base charge + energy charge)
Equipment-based residential time-of-day service requiring thermal storage and approved controls
Residential time-of-use pilot: enrollment status and product publication date
Residential critical-peak pilot: enrollment status and event conditions
May 2026 domestic and MURB89 tariffs, dated conditional pilots, FAM/DSM/storm and optional Solar Garden/Community Solar riders
Business rates page with Rate 10, 11, 12 (small commercial, commercial general, large commercial)

utilities.notes: Ten live records include standard/TOD/conditional pilots, MURB house-meter TOU89, separate optional Solar Garden and Community Solar adjustments, and existing business10/11/12. MURB requires ten units, its own General/MURB rider rows and minimum-bill context; printed Note1 explicitly applies the peak price on weekends/holidays. Solar credits apply only to subscriber-attributed generation with base tariffs still separate. Pilot restoration status remains conditional; no early November/2027 prices. Other building business classes and rider/date coverage still need audit.

utilities.name: Maritime Electric

sources.description: Rates and General Rules and Regulations — IRAC-approved Schedule of Adjusted Rates (PDF)
Section N-28 Schedule of Adjusted Rates effective August 1, 2026 (PDF)

utilities.notes: Maritime Electric is the primary electricity distributor in Prince Edward Island, a subsidiary of Fortis Inc. Regulated by the Island Regulatory and Appeals Commission (IRAC). Building classes 110/130/131/133/232/233 are source-checked with per-class fail-closed parsing and a source fixture. Industrial 310/320/330/340 are retained as reference. Lighting and short-term service are excluded. No recurring riders are published.

utilities.name: Newfoundland Power

sources.description: Electricity rates page with links to PDF rate schedules
RateBook effective July 1, 2026 (PDF)

utilities.notes: Newfoundland Power is a subsidiary of Fortis Inc. and the primary electricity distributor on the island of Newfoundland. Regulated by the Newfoundland and Labrador Board of Commissioners of Public Utilities (PUB). Rates available only in linked PDF 'Schedule of Rates, Rules and Regulations'. The July 1, 2026 RateBook also supplies Domestic Seasonal 1.1S adjustments, the prompt-payment discount (-1.5%), primary-voltage demand discounts and service fees (reconnection/application/dishonoured payment). Municipal tax and RSP riders are already embedded in printed rates. Curtailable and lighting service are excluded.

utilities.name: NL Hydro

sources.description: Current electricity rates page with inline rates and PDF link (note: 'electicity' typo is in the real URL)
July 2026 Schedule of Rates: Island/Labrador/diesel domestic and general-service, government distinctions, Burgeo school/library and two seasonal adjustment options

utilities.notes: Eighteen current building-service and seasonal-option records are parsed from individually dated July 2026 pages. Phase/amperage basic charges are mutually exclusive alternatives. kW/kVA, monthly diesel blocks, government/non-government service, required minimum/maximum bills and optional adjustment conditions are retained. Seasonal options require their base schedule; no bill totals. Lighting/wholesale are outside scope; net-metering, commissioning and contract-specific industrial applicability remain explicit catalogue gaps.

Detailed 1160/2160 base PDFs are image-only; broader building classes and Rider A need OCR or authoritative text alternatives. General-service and representative diesel fallbacks remain unverified.
